walkthroughs.body_html: Positive balance (accumulation > ablation) drives advance; negative balance triggers retreat. Greenland Ice Sheet lost about 280 Gt/yr (2003-2018). Globally, glaciers lost about 9 trillion tonnes 1961-2016, contributing 27 mm to sea level rise.

Warm-based glaciers in temperate Alps slide on basal meltwater at 50-300 m/yr. Cold-based glaciers in Antarctica move at 1-10 m/yr through internal deformation alone. Surge events can briefly reach 100 m/day.

Greenland outlet glacier doubled flow speed from 6 km/yr (1990s) to over 12 km/yr (2003). Calving front retreated 40 km since 1850. Drains 7 percent of Greenland Ice Sheet, contributing to 4 percent of global sea level rise.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an ice age and a glacial period?
options: Ice ages happen every winter when it gets cold.
An ice age is a long era with permanent ice on Earth (we are still in one); within it, glacial periods (cold) alternate with interglacials (warm) every ~100,000 years driven by Milankovitch cycles.
The ice age ended 10,000 years ago.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.

mcqs.q: Why are there no volcanoes at conservative plate boundaries?
options: Ice ages happen every winter when it gets cold.
There are no volcanoes because the boundaries are too cold.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
Conservative boundaries involve plates sliding past each other horizontally — no crust is created or destroyed, so there is no subduction to generate magma.
